result.title: Soft Ontology Priors over Latent Concept Posteriors for Weakly Supervised Neuro-Symbolic Learning
result.summary: Neuro-symbolic (NeSy) predictors that supervise only the task label suffer from reasoning shortcuts: distinct concept mappings achieve the same maximum likelihood, leaving the recovered concepts unidentifiable and unsafe for downstream reuse. We attack this failure by injecting a soft ontology prior over the latent concepts into the training objective and compiling it together with the task constraint into a smooth, decomposable probabilistic circuit. Under independent Bernoulli perception, the normalisers of the resulting structured concept posterior reduce to weighted model counts that are linear in the compiled circuit size, because the neural leaf weights fold into the circuit before evaluation. The soft compilation strategy places expert axioms in the circuit's weights rather than its support (task-structural axioms guaranteed by the data-generating process stay hard), so noisy expert axioms only redistribute prior mass and cannot empty the support. We characterise how the prior reweights label-restricted shortcut mass through differences in ontology violation energy, show that soft priors incur bounded log-density perturbations under bounded axiom noise, and prove that the hard-support counterpart can be made degenerate by a single corrupted axiom. We validate these predictions on an audited six-concept view of the real-world BDD-OIA driving benchmark and on controlled NeSy tasks.

AI.brief_summary: 论文针对弱监督神经符号学习中的「推理捷径」——只在任务标签监督下潜概念不可辨识——在潜概念后验上注入软本体先验，与任务约束一同编译为可分解概率电路，并给出先验重加权捷径质量、有界噪声下对数密度扰动等分析，在 BDD-OIA 驾驶基准与受控任务上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「任务标签正确但潜概念不可辨识」的诊断与软先验正则，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态是否真正承载视觉证据、以及轨迹监督下的贡献分配提供可核查的借鉴，但静态概念与 Bernoulli 感知设定离推理期状态生成较远。
